questions.title: How does appellate court apply a ‘substantial‑evidence’ standard when reviewing a Board’s denial under § 1252(b)(4)(A)?
questions.question_body:
"In Jimenez v. Bondi" the court said it reviews BIA findings under a substantial‑evidence standard **only** insofar as the record supports those findings – it didn’t conduct a de novo rebalance.
I’m struggling with what counts as substantial evidence in an immigration‑doctrine setting versus simple administrative fact finding.
When looking at the IJ’s record versus what happened on appeal, how should I decide whether testimony supports “reasonable adjudicators” versus suppression based on judicial discretion?

questions.title: "Threats alone don’t rise to past persecution" ‑ How much intimidation actually fulfills INA’s past‑persecution element?

"The IJ held that John Jimenez’s phone calls, brochure scare tactics and house break‑ins were insufficient even when viewed collectively," yet Netherlands courts sometimes award relief for persistent threats.
What distinguishes intimidation that “does rise” from intimidation that doesn’t?
How do things like physical harm versus psychological trauma play in assessing whether suffering is offensive enough?
